passage: Kalyani sat on the charpai in the courtyard, feeding the newborn while her two-year-old son Rituraj hovered at the edge, thumb in his mouth. All morning Rituraj had heard only "good helper, well done." Now Kalyani patted the space beside her and pulled him up. "You're still my big boy, always," she said, and tucked his head under her chin. "There's room in my lap for both of you." Rituraj let out a long breath, took his thumb out, and stayed, watching the baby's tiny fist.

qa.q: Where was Kalyani sitting while she fed the newborn?
qa.a: Kalyani was sitting on the charpai in the courtyard.

qa.q: What was Rituraj probably feeling when he let out a long breath in his mother's lap?
qa.a: He probably felt relief and safety, sensing that his mother's love had not been used up by the baby. 🙂

qa.q: Why did the words and the lap help more than being called a good helper?
qa.a: Praise for helping only speaks to what he does, while being held and told he is always her big boy tells him he is loved for himself.

qa.q: How might Kalyani have felt, sitting between a newborn and an anxious toddler?
qa.a: She may have felt pulled two ways and wanted both children to know they had a place with her.

grounding: Shows a toddler being cuddled and told he is still his mother's big boy after a new baby arrives, so love feels secure.
